task: Two pixel-art cinematic storyboard sheets, eight planning frames, no video generation or game implementation

A.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a NEW visual cinematic storyboard contact sheet for the existing Clockwork pixel-art game, NOT an animation spritesheet and NOT actual gameplay screenshots. Generate ONE coherent 2x2 storyboard page with FOUR equal landscape 16:9 frames, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, separated by neat dark gutters. All panels must be large, legible cinematic film stills in deliberate crisp low-resolution pixel art; visible square pixels, stepped edges, limited navy/steel/brass/cyan/red palette, no smooth painted illustration or photorealism. It is a storyboard preview, not final game art.
Input images are REFERENCE ONLY, not edit targets:
1 is approved guardian idle design. 2 is the same guardian with the RED circular core visible INSIDE its open angular steel pressure jaws. 3 is the approved small Tique. 4 is the actual side-view battle scene defining proportions, floor, positions and background style. 5 defines the actual gray connected walls, handled brass square weight, cyan round orb, and recessed square and circular sockets.
Subject invariants: Tique is the same SMALL brass robot, round brass head, two cyan circular eyes and cyan heart chest, same proportions as reference 3. The guardian is the same DARK STEEL quadruped with FOUR short mechanical legs, angular pressure-jaw head, rivets and pistons, red internal jaw/core. The guardian has NO EYES, NO LENS, NO HUMAN FACE, no horns, no new anatomy; its red core is inside its mouth, never an eye on the head. Keep the steel silhouette in refs 1 and 2 and the boss-to-Tique scale in ref 4. Tique stays on the LEFT of the side-view arena, guardian stays on the RIGHT facing LEFT. No human or extra character.
Panel A1 (top left): close overhead/oblique view of the LAST handled brass square weight seated into its recessed square socket, matching ref 5's exact silhouettes and materials. A restrained amber connection glow. Gray floor and machinery, a trace of cyan cabling. A clear tactile successful docking, not a magic orb replacing the weight.
Panel A2 (top right): macro cinematic crop of existing-style brass/steel power relay and cable junction in the dark factory; a CYAN electrical indicator has just lit, and a thin cyan light travels along one cable. The mechanical geometry is solid and plausible, composed for a tiny camera push. This shot conveys power reaching the guardian.
Panel A3 (bottom left): close-up of the SAME guardian's angular steel pressure jaws and pistons from refs 1/2; the red internal circular core is beginning to glow, teeth/steel pressure plates and one compressed piston visible. The head has no eyes. Controlled dark navy atmosphere, red internal core as the sole threat accent. This is quiet awakening, not an attack or explosion.
Panel A4 (bottom right): return-to-game SIDE VIEW wide arena very close to ref 4's camera and layout, no HUD. Tique small at the left on the floor, the same four-legged guardian at the right facing Tique, mouth red; side pylons and dark mechanical factory arches. A clear playable horizontal space between them. This frame must look like the existing pixel-art game, not a new third-person perspective.
Text: ONLY small exact labels "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4" on their corresponding panel top-left corners, unobtrusive off-white pixel lettering. No titles, captions, dialogue, logos, watermarks, UI bars, arrows or extra text.
Emotional progression: success -> power returns -> unexpected threat -> player control. Avoid exaggerated glow, beams obscuring silhouettes, distorted robot joints, smooth gradients, painterly surfaces, new boss design.

B.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a NEW visual cinematic storyboard contact sheet for the existing Clockwork pixel-art game, NOT an animation spritesheet and NOT actual gameplay screenshots. Generate ONE coherent 2x2 storyboard page with FOUR equal landscape 16:9 frames, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, separated by neat dark gutters. All panels are large readable film stills in deliberate crisp low-resolution PIXEL ART; visible square pixels, stepped contours, limited steel/navy/brass/cyan palette and gentle amber warmth. Match the reference game's pixel density and material language. No smooth painted illustration, 3D rendering or photorealism. This is a storyboard preview, not final game art.
Input images are REFERENCE ONLY:
1 is approved Tique, same small round brass robot, two CYAN circular eyes and CYAN heart chest; preserve its small limbs and round head exactly. 2 is approved guardian anatomy, DARK STEEL quadruped, FOUR short mechanical legs and angular steel pressure jaws, NO EYES/no human face. 3 is the approved right-hand exit door architecture: brass/steel frame. 4 is the actual side-view battle camera, floor, arena arches and relative scale. 5 is the existing factory/workshop material language: dark steel panels, brass piping, round gear clock, cyan lights. Do not copy HUD text/bars from reference 4.
Panel B1 (top left): SIDE VIEW arena after victory, same camera and horizontal floor as reference 4. The approved four-legged guardian is grounded and powered down in its existing silhouette, red jaw light extinguished. Small Tique stands on the left, relaxed not heroic battle pose. No mutilation, no explosion, no loot. Machinery light is calmer.
Panel B2 (top right): SIDE VIEW game handoff at the RIGHT exit door matching reference 3, now OPEN; the SAME small brass Tique in three-quarter/side orientation immediately outside the doorway, going LEFT TO RIGHT toward gentle AMBER warmth inside. Preserve his cyan eyes and chest heart, small proportions. The door is tangible steel/brass with no fantasy portal vortex. Dark factory behind him.
Panel B3 (bottom left): quiet establishing wide interior of the implied Elias workshop on the OTHER SIDE of that doorway. No people and no new NPC. A humble mechanical workshop, one worn steel/brass workbench, a warm amber task lamp, a round wall clock/gear clock, restrained tools and pipes matching reference 5's industrial design, cyan indicator accents. It feels sheltered and lived-in, not a lavish new fantasy town. Keep a restrained visible pixel grid, clear shapes, and cinematic negative space.
Panel B4 (bottom right): a tighter framed still of the SAME workbench, task lamp and round clock from B3, one continuous location not a redesigned room. Amber light falls on a place at the bench; a few sparse dust pixels float in the light. No new character, no robot duplication. Enough quiet empty space for a later ENGINE-rendered ending caption, but do NOT draw that caption. Warm, modest homecoming, no grand finale.
Text: ONLY small exact labels "B1", "B2", "B3", "B4" on the corresponding panel top-left corners, unobtrusive off-white pixel lettering. No other text, dialogue, logos, titles, watermarks, arrows or HUD.
Emotional progression: quiet relief -> threshold -> familiar warmth -> belonging. Avoid lens flare, blurry bloom, hyper-detailed photorealism, warped robot parts, new guardian eyes, humans, oversized Tique, cyberpunk neon, magic beams, smooth gradients.
